Hi all —

Thanks Stephanie and Maya. I reviewed the attached Exhibit C and put together a redline (attached: HelioHealth_ExhibitC_Redline_v3.docx) plus a short summary below.

Summary of proposed legal edits (high level):
- Consolidation: Replace the three line-items with a single "Consolidated GPU Capacity" SKU. Define unit as "GPU-hour" and include a clause that allows customer-directed reallocation between pool types up to the committed monthly capacity without a change order, provided aggregate committed capacity stays the same.
- Tax passthrough: Insert clause: "Customer is responsible for all applicable taxes (including VAT/GST) arising from the use of the Service. Redwood shall invoice net of VAT/GST where Customer provides a valid tax exemption certificate; otherwise taxes will be added to the invoice in accordance with applicable law." Also include an obligation for customer to provide VAT registration / tax ID for intra-EU reverse charge where applicable.
- Implementation exhibit: Clarify effective date for consolidated SKU and whether billing for the new SKU starts on the next invoice cycle or is prorated for the month of change.

Pricing impact (Finance input requested):
- The consolidation itself does not automatically increase unit cost, but removing per-pool buffers and adding administrative flexibility triggers a modest commercial adjustment. My recommendation to preserve capacity reservation economics is a one-time 2% uplift on the consolidated unit price (applies to committed units only), with existing overage rates unchanged. This is a negotiable point — Laura, please confirm if 2% is workable operationally.

Process rec: once HelioHealth confirms acceptance of the redline, Redwood will:
1) generate a clean Order Form reflecting the consolidated SKU and the 2% uplift (if accepted),
2) route for internal legal and sales approval,
3) send DocuSign envelope to HelioHealth.

I attached the redline with tracked changes and a short snippet of suggested legal text (see paragraph 6.3 on tax).
